free_tier.stated: USD 49/year, renewing at USD 49/year with the price locked until cancellation or a plan change, for 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM and 5 TB of monthly transfer, annual billing only. Disk differs by site: 120 GB of NVMe in Dallas on an AMD EPYC 7543P with a 4 Gbps port, 80 GB in Amsterdam on an EPYC 7C13 with a 2.5 Gbps port, and 80 GB in New York on dual Xeon Gold 6138 with a 2.5 Gbps port. Every site includes a dedicated IPv4, a routed /64 IPv6, DDoS protection and a 99.9 percent SLA with service credits; stock is capped at 40 units in Dallas and 15 in each of the other two.

egress.terms: 5 TB a month; no overage price and no post-allowance throttle stated

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: the vendor page describes provisioning 'from the control panel in about a minute' without naming the panel; it publishes a looking glass, and the thread gives a status page at status.d4networks.com, an ASN of its own (AS14475) and a /22 from ARIN. No API or CLI is documented on either page read
chaining: USD 49 a year for 4 GB and 120 GB with 5 TB a month, a locked renewal price and a 99.9 percent credit-backed SLA is the best-evidenced cheap plan, and the Dallas row carries 50 percent more disk than the other two at the same price the published Geekbench runs (1758 single in Dallas against 1148 in New York) make the site choice a measurable decision rather than a guess

limits.value: 5 TB a month counts against both directions by implication of the plan table, and it is the wall before the 4 Gbps Dallas port: 5 TB a month averages about 15 Mbit/s. No overage price and no post-allowance throttle are stated. The record also carries an unusual contractual limit: the annual price is fixed by the terms until cancellation, which is why the renewal rate is knowable here and not on most records.

the vendor homepage confirms the three regions and the port classes ('Cloud VPS on ports up to 5 Gbps' for New York, 'up to 10 Gbps' for Dallas, 'up to 5 Gbps' for Amsterdam) and states 'A 99.9% uptime guarantee, backed by service credits', but carries no plan table and no price
